note: source: attacker-controlled 'sfnt' type record supplies a non-zero resource-array offset (resourcesZ) pointing at a 12-byte ResourceRecord whose 24-bit data offset is 0xFFFFFF, far beyond the blob, so deep validation is doomed to fail.

root cause: resourcesZ is a null-enabled OffsetTo (has_null=true); when deep validation of the ResourceRecord array fails, neuter() zeroes the offset instead of rejecting the blob, and the second sanitize round then passes with 0 edits so the blob is accepted.
dataLen==0 makes the resource data block empty; the data offset stays fixed at 256 (the dfont tag value), so an OpenTypeFontFace formed at data_base+4 lands near the end of the 260-byte blob.
the first sfnt type record is selected (idx 0 < resCountM1+1); resourcesZ is now 0, so the resource record is resolved through the null branch.
the zeroed resourcesZ is null, so OffsetTo::operator() returns Null(UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord>); the all-zero ResourceRecord yields offset24==0.

with offset24==0 (has_null=false so zero is not null), the forged OpenTypeFontFace header is formed at data_base+4 = 260; this header was never sanitized because the null resource record bypassed deep validation.
sink: loading the table count (BinSearchHeader.len, 2 bytes) of the forged header at 260+4=264; the read [264,266) crosses the 260-byte heap allocation -> heap-buffer-overflow read of size 2.
